title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 351 (Liquidator not to deposit monies into private banking account)

content.overview: Neither the Official Liquidator nor the Company Liquidator of a company shall deposit any monies received by him in his capacity as such into any private banking account.
content.glance: Official Liquidator and Company Liquidator must not deposit liquidation monies into any private banking account.
content.study: Section 351 is an absolute prohibition. Neither the Official Liquidator nor the Company Liquidator may deposit monies received in that capacity into any private banking account. Funds must be held in the public account (Official Liquidator) or the special scheduled-bank account (Company Liquidator) as required by ss. 349–350.

sections.heading: Prohibition
sections.body: No deposit of liquidation monies into any private banking account by Official Liquidator or Company Liquidator.

provisions.title: Liquidator not to deposit monies into private banking account

examples.title: Private account breach
examples.body: A Company Liquidator parks realisations in his personal savings account. He violates s. 351.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 351 allow temporary parking in a private account?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The prohibition is absolute; monies must not be deposited into any private banking account.

rows.left: Liquidator not to deposit monies into private banking account

misconceptions.trap: Temporary private parking is permitted for operational convenience.
misconceptions.correction: Section 351 forbids deposit into any private banking account.
